messages:
Olivia: FYI — seeing a spike of 502/521 errs from eu-west customers since ~08:10 UTC. It looks like the ALB is returning the wrong cert for some handshakes :confused:
Sam: Any listener or cert changes this morning?
Olivia: We rotated a wildcard cert on Friday, and added a few host-based listener rules. Curious thing: failures only from a handful of corporate NAT subnets.
Raj: Can you paste an access log line and a quick curl or s_client output?
Olivia: ALB access: "2026-03-15T08:12:34.123Z alb-id request-id 10.0.1.45:443 10.0.4.57:52322 - - 502 502 0 123 0 0 "GET /health HTTP/1.1"
curl -v --resolve example.redwood.ai:443:54.23.12.9 https://example.redwood.ai/health shows cert: CN=default-edge, not example.redwood.ai
Sam: That smells like missing/empty SNI on ClientHello or ALB picking the default action when SNI not present. Clients behind some proxies reuse TLS sessions or strip SNI in some cases. Have we seen any mTLS or proxy-protocol config changes?
Olivia: No mTLS changes. These corporate proxies appear to multiplex many hostnames on one TLS session. openssl s_client -connect lb:443 -servername example.redwood.ai worked from my laptop, but from a repro machine behind the corp proxy the servername is absent and we get default cert.
Raj: ALB uses SNI from ClientHello to pick the certificate/target group if the listener has multiple certificates. If ClientHello has no SNI (or session resumption without SNI), ALB falls back to default cert. Two mitigations:
  - Make the default cert intentionally unrouteable (fixed-response 421) so clients clearly fail fast instead of silently getting wrong cert.
  - Add higher-priority host-header listener rules that return the right backend or fixed-response rather than relying solely on SNI-based cert selection.
Sam: Another option is to switch to TCP passthrough (NLB -> nginx ingress) for affected hostnames so the ingress can inspect the real SNI on each new connection, or use dedicated ALB listeners per hostname (scales poorly).
Olivia: For immediate mitigation I rolled back the wildcard to include explicit SAN entries for the known hostnames in eu-west and created a temporary listener rule that does host-header match with a fixed-response 421 as the default action. Rolling now.
infra-bot: Triggered pipeline: roll-back-wildcard-eu-west #3421 (in-progress) :rocket:
Sam: Also capture ClientHello info in TCP dumps and enable additional ALB logging (TLS handshake times and SNI logging if available) — will open a short runbook to detect SNI-less clients proactively.
Olivia: Thanks. Opening an incident and will post updates here. If the rollback doesn't cut it we'll consider moving the problematic customers to a dedicated listener.
Sam: ping @Raj to follow up on a long-term fix: either ingress-controller changes or switch to NLB passthrough for corp proxies.
Raj: Will dig into flow logs and see if NAT port reuse or session reuse is the root cause.
Olivia: Great, thanks everyone.
